verdict.summary: Equinox has crossed into senior-producer scale, but the merger makes the current quarter a poor proxy for the combined company. Q2 pre-merger revenue was $769.8 million on 176,836 gold ounces, with $358.3 million adjusted EBITDA and $230.6 million GAAP net income. Following the July 31 Orla combination, management raised 2026 production guidance to 870,000-920,000 ounces, with consolidated AISC of $1,900-$2,000 per ounce and $600-$650 million growth capital. The transaction added Musselwhite and Camino Rojo, issued exactly 378,115,579 shares and produced a stated pro forma $214 million net-cash position excluding convertibles. Growth is credible but expensive: Valentine Phase 2 carries a $436 million initial budget, South Railroad requires about $395 million and first gold is targeted for 2028. Q2 all-operations AISC was already $2,175 per ounce, leaving execution sensitivity despite high realized gold. A B grade is defensible for scale and liquidity, but integration, incomplete purchase accounting and capex keep the setup in Wait until the existing $13.56 completed-bar and volume gate confirms. Value the combined asset portfolio, not backward-looking EPS alone.

business.overview:
Equinox earns revenue by producing and selling gold across Greenstone, Valentine, Nicaragua, Mesquite and, after the Orla merger, Musselwhite and Camino Rojo. Q2 production was 176,836 ounces; realized gold price, recovery, grade, AISC and growth capital determine cash generation. After the transaction, stated pro forma liquidity was $1.214B, but Valentine Phase 2 and South Railroad carry about $831M of combined initial budgets.

The AI transmission channel is remote: gold benefits mainly from monetary demand, real rates and risk hedging rather than data-center construction. AI can support broader power and capital spending, but it is not a measurable revenue driver for Equinox and should not inflate mine valuation.

The model breaks if Greenstone or Valentine ramps miss plan, integration fails, gold prices fall toward $1,900-$2,000 guidance AISC, or simultaneous Valentine and South Railroad spending consumes liquidity. Share issuance and convertible claims can also dilute otherwise successful production growth.
business.moat: Equinox's moat is a geographically concentrated North American portfolio with operating infrastructure and a permitted growth pipeline. Musselwhite, Camino Rojo, Greenstone and Valentine create scale; South Railroad and expansions add duration, but execution and capital discipline determine whether scarce ore bodies translate into per-share value.

Production was 176,836 ounces at $1,816 cash cost and $2,175 AISC. Post-merger guidance is 870,000-920,000 ounces at $1,900-$2,000 AISC with $600-$650M growth capital. The caveat is comparability: Q2 excludes Orla, while guidance includes only five months of Musselwhite and Camino Rojo and substantial new capex.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: The July 31 Orla combination issued 378,115,579 Equinox common shares, a completed merger issuance rather than shelf capacity. Management stated pro forma net cash of $214M excluding convertibles and $1.214B liquidity, but project commitments are large: $436M Valentine Phase 2 and approximately $395M South Railroad. The 1.17B post-merger snapshot is a basic denominator; because convertibles and awards are not reconciled into a current fully diluted bridge, enterprise value is stated as at least $15.52B and no diluted per-share NAV is claimed. This limitation is part of the B grade and wait state.

filingsReview.summary: 4 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade B measures fundamentals; trade state wait measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The July 31 6-K reports completion of the Orla merger and issuance of exactly 378,115,579 Equinox common shares as consideration, leaving legacy Equinox and former Orla holders at approximately 67% and 33%; this is completed primary merger consideration, not shelf, ATM or debt capacity.

The August 5 6-K supplies Q2 financial statements and the subsequent-event merger accounting: 378,115,579 shares had approximately $3.6B fair value, ownership became about 67%/33%, and purchase-price allocation remained incomplete; it also supports the pre-merger quarter's results and comparability warning.
The 2025 Form 40-F provides the pre-merger reserve, mine concentration, jurisdiction and capital baseline; it cannot alone represent the combined Orla portfolio or post-merger share count.
The August 17 6-K supports South Railroad's positive federal Record of Decision, approximately $395M initial capital and 2028 first-gold target; it is a permitting milestone, not current revenue.

contrarianRisks: The Orla merger issued 378.1M shares; this is completed consideration and must enter every per-share comparison.
Q2 results exclude Orla while full-year guidance includes five months, limiting simple annualization.
Pro forma net cash excludes convertible debentures and estimated transaction costs expected in Q3.
Valentine Phase 2 and South Railroad require approximately $831M combined initial capital.
South Railroad's positive Record of Decision advances permitting but is not construction completion or operating revenue.

macro.impact: EQX is a high-operating-leverage gold producer: real rates and monetary demand drive realized gold, while diesel, labor and currencies drive AISC. The Orla merger broadens North American mine exposure; AI has no direct earnings channel and should not enter the base valuation.

risks.riskSummary: Equinox must integrate a much larger portfolio while funding two major projects; high gold prices and stated net cash help, but $831M of project budgets, new shares, convertibles and elevated AISC create substantial per-share execution risk. Retail war-room: gold, merger-integration or permit news can gap EQX through $13.265; regular-session liquidity still carries opening spread and slippage, so trim sizing for project-event risk, avoid earnings and construction decisions, and never chase above the $14.0799 first resistance.

tradeIdea.thesis: The wait setup expresses successful Orla integration and delivery toward 870,000-920,000 ounces only after $13.56 confirms with the existing volume condition, with the final $13.265 August 27 pivot stop controlling downside. EQX must clear supply at the dated $14.0799 and $15.2899 mine-integration checkpoints. Improving AISC, preserved liquidity and disciplined project capital remain mandatory; permit milestones cannot substitute for durable per-share cash flow.
